lesson.subject: anatomy
lesson.title: Orbit, eyeball and visual pathway
lesson.summary: The orbit has a superior roof, medial wall, floor and lateral wall surrounding the globe and extraocular muscles.
lesson.section: 21. CN I and CN II; 22. CN III, IV, and VI

steps.title: CN I and CN II
steps.body:
CN I olfactory nerve carries smell fibers from olfactory mucosa through cribriform plate to olfactory bulb. CN II optic nerve carries vision from retina through optic canal to optic chiasm and optic tract.

Olfactory fibers pass through cribriform plate of ethmoid. Olfactory nerve has no brainstem nucleus. Optic nerve is an extension of diencephalon and is covered by meninges. Optic canal transmits optic nerve and ophthalmic artery. Nasal retinal fibers cross at optic chiasm; temporal retinal fibers remain ipsilateral.

steps.title: CN III, IV, and VI
steps.body:
Oculomotor, trochlear, and abducent nerves control extraocular muscles. CN III also carries parasympathetic fibers to ciliary ganglion for pupillary constriction and accommodation.

CN III exits interpeduncular fossa and enters orbit through superior orbital fissure. Trochlear fibers cross before their dorsal exit below the inferior colliculus and supply the contralateral superior oblique relative to their nucleus. CN VI exits pontomedullary junction and supplies lateral rectus. CN III supplies levator palpebrae superioris, superior rectus, medial rectus, inferior rectus, and inferior oblique. Parasympathetic CN III fibers synapse in ciliary ganglion and travel via short ciliary nerves.

steps.title: Why distinguish extraocular movement from pupillary and lens control?
steps.body: Extraocular skeletal muscles rotate the globe through III, IV and VI motor pathways. Pupillary constriction and lens accommodation use parasympathetic III fibers synapsing in the ciliary ganglion before reaching smooth-muscle targets. Sympathetic pathways dilate the pupil through a different route. Visual sensory signals travel through II. An eye can therefore have a visual, ocular-motor or autonomic deficit with different anatomical localization. Calling all of these functions eye movement loses the essential distinction between sensory input and motor outputs.

steps.title: Apply the anatomy and resolve a common confusion
steps.body: The orbit has a superior roof, medial wall, floor and lateral wall surrounding the globe and extraocular muscles. Its medial wall and floor are relatively thin and border ethmoidal and maxillary spaces. The globe has an outer fibrous coat, vascular middle coat and neural retina. Light passes through cornea, aqueous, pupil, lens and vitreous before reaching retina; neural signals leave through the optic nerve. Nasal retinal fibers cross at the chiasm, while temporal fibers do not.
